subject: physics
title: Circular Motion & Gravitation Adventure 2: Newton's law of gravitation and orbits
welcome_lead: Today you'll orbit a planet with F = GMm/r².
meta_desc: Physics — Newton's gravity F = GMm/r², orbital speed, Kepler's 3rd law T² ∝ r³.
final_note: You learned F = GMm/r², g = GM/r², orbital v = √(GM/r), Kepler's 3rd law T² = 4π²r³/(GM).

walkthroughs.body_html:
F = G M m / r²

G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg². Same law for falling apple + orbiting moon (Newton, 1687).

Gravitational field strength:

g = F/m = GM/r²

Earth surface: M = 6.0×10²⁴ kg, r = 6.4×10⁶ m → g = 9.8 N/kg.

Gravity provides centripetal force: GMm/r² = mv²/r.

v = √(GM/r)

So T = 2πr/v = 2π√(r³/GM).

Squaring: T² = 4π²r³/(GM) — Kepler's 3rd law T² ∝ r³.

Geostationary: T = 24 h (86,400 s); above equator. Solve for r ≈ 4.2 × 10⁷ m from centre (~36,000 km altitude). Used for TV, weather.

Escape velocity: from energy ½mv² = GMm/r → v_esc = √(2GM/r). Earth: 11.2 km/s.

For black holes, v_esc > c → light cannot escape.

mcqs.q: If air resistance is ignored, which falls faster: a heavy ball or a light ball dropped from the same height?
options: Heavier objects fall faster than lighter objects because gravity pulls more on them.
Photon energy depends on how fast the photon is moving relative to the source.
Both fall at the same rate because gravitational acceleration is independent of mass.
The lighter ball falls faster because it has less inertia.

mcqs.q: What determines the energy of a single photon?
options: Photon energy depends on how fast the photon is moving relative to the source.
A brighter light has higher-energy photons because intensity makes each photon more energetic.
The number of turns in the coil alone.
Its frequency (E = hf) — only frequency, not intensity.

mcqs.q: According to Faraday's law, what determines the size of the induced emf in a coil?
options: The strength of the magnetic field alone.
The rate of change of magnetic flux linkage through the coil.
The number of turns in the coil alone.
The lighter ball falls faster because it has less inertia.
